ancestral roots = the origins of your family in earlier generations
cultural roots = the traditions and history that shape who you are
social standing = a person's rank or status in society
national identity = the feeling of belonging to a particular nation
sense of belonging = the feeling that you are accepted as part of a group
dual nationality = the legal status of being a citizen of two countries
overprotective parent = a mother or father who tries to remove every risk from a child's life
self-discovery = the process of learning what kind of person you are
generation gap = a difference in attitudes between younger and older people
extended family = relatives beyond parents and children, such as aunts and grandparents
only child = a person with no brothers or sisters
country of origin = the country where a person or their family comes from
mother tongue = the first language a person learns at home
bilingual = able to speak two languages fluently
lineage = direct descent from a particular ancestor or family
forebear = a person from whom you are descended
chosen family = people who are not relatives but give you the support of a family
adopted child = a child legally taken into a family that is not biologically their own
biological parent = the mother or father related to a child by birth
single-parent household = a home in which one parent raises the children
core beliefs = the deepest ideas that shape how you judge right and wrong
social background = the class, education and circumstances you grow up in
privileged upbringing = a childhood with wealth, connections or other advantages
humble origins = a family background with little money or status
role model = a person whose behaviour others want to copy
peer group = people of a similar age who influence one another
maiden name = a woman's surname before marriage
place of origin = the town, region or country you come from
emotional intelligence = the ability to understand and manage feelings
formative years = the period of youth that strongly shapes character
complexion = the natural colour and quality of the skin on the face
sallow complexion = skin that looks yellowish and unhealthy
weathered skin = skin that looks rough from age, sun or outdoor work
youthful appearance = looking younger than your actual age
premature ageing = looking or becoming old earlier than is typical
well-groomed = clean, neat and carefully looked after in appearance
unkempt = untidy; not looked after, especially hair or clothes
striking features = facial characteristics that immediately attract attention
distinctive features = unusual or easily recognised parts of someone's appearance
athletic build = a body shape that looks fit and strong from sport
slender figure = a thin, graceful body shape
petite = small and slim, usually used of a woman
burly = large, strong and heavily built
gaunt = very thin, especially in the face, often from illness or stress
frail = physically weak, often because of age or illness
receding hairline = hair that is gradually disappearing from the forehead
greying temples = grey hair appearing at the sides of the forehead
stubble = very short beard hair that has not been shaved for a day or two
clean-shaven = with no beard or moustache
posture = the way you hold your back and shoulders when sitting or standing
gait = the particular way a person walks
bear a resemblance to = to look similar to another person
inherit a trait = to get a quality from a parent through genes or example
cosmetic surgery = medical operations intended to change appearance rather than treat illness
makeover = a complete change of hairstyle, clothes or appearance
body image = how you see and feel about the way your body looks
self-conscious = too aware of yourself and worried about being judged
ageing gracefully = growing older without desperately hiding the signs of age
facial hair = hair growing on the face, such as a beard or stubble
personal grooming = the habits of keeping yourself clean and tidy
conscientious = careful to do your work thoroughly and honestly
absent-minded = often forgetting things because your mind is on something else
open-minded = willing to consider new ideas and other people's views
narrow-minded = unwilling to accept ideas or behaviour different from your own
tactful = careful not to say things that will upset or embarrass others
tactless = likely to say things that upset people, without intending to
assertive = confident in stating your opinions without being aggressive
submissive = too ready to obey others and not express your own views
stubborn = determined not to change your mind, even when you should
determined = having a strong desire to succeed and not giving up easily
resourceful = good at finding practical solutions with limited means
impulsive = acting suddenly without thinking about the consequences
level-headed = calm and sensible, even in a difficult situation
hot-tempered = becoming angry quickly and easily
easy-going = relaxed and not easily upset or worried
outgoing = friendly and enjoying the company of other people
withdrawn = very quiet and not wanting to communicate with others
reserved = slow to show feelings or opinions
two-faced = nice to someone in public but unkind or dishonest behind their back
trustworthy = able to be relied on to be honest and keep secrets
deceitful = behaving in a dishonest way in order to trick people
conceited = too proud of your abilities or appearance
humble = not proud; not thinking you are better than others
considerate = careful not to cause inconvenience or hurt to others
charismatic = having a personality that attracts and influences others
timid = shy and easily frightened; lacking confidence
resilient = able to recover quickly from difficulties
witty = able to say clever, amusing things quickly
inquisitive = eager to find out about things; asking many questions
aloof = not friendly or willing to take part; emotionally distant
resentment = a bitter feeling that you have been treated unfairly
elation = a feeling of great happiness and excitement
humiliation = a strong feeling of shame after being made to look foolish
anguish = severe mental or emotional pain
despair = the complete loss of hope
contentment = quiet happiness with what you have
nostalgia = a bittersweet longing for a time in the past
remorse = deep regret for something wrong you have done
envy = the unhappy feeling of wanting what someone else has
contempt = the feeling that someone or something is worthless
indignation = anger because something seems unfair or wrong
apprehension = anxiety about something that may happen
exhilaration = a feeling of excitement and energy
grief = intense sorrow, especially after a death or serious loss
relief = the comfortable feeling when something unpleasant stops or does not happen
frustration = annoyed disappointment because you cannot achieve something
disappointment = sadness because something was not as good as you hoped
embarrassment = a feeling of awkward shame in front of others
astonishment = great surprise
bitterness = lasting anger and disappointment about unfair treatment
longing = a strong wish for someone or something you do not have
dread = great fear about something that will happen
mixed feelings = both positive and negative emotions about the same thing
come to terms with = to accept a difficult situation and learn to live with it
bottle up = to hide your feelings instead of expressing them
take something to heart = to be deeply affected by criticism or a remark
lose your temper = to become suddenly very angry
keep your composure = to stay calm and in control of your behaviour
overwhelmed = feeling unable to cope because there is too much to deal with
guilt-ridden = feeling guilty to an extreme, constant degree
self-esteem = confidence in your own worth and abilities
self-worth = the sense that you deserve respect, independent of success
identity crisis = a period of confusion about who you are and what you want
self-awareness = knowledge of your own character, feelings and motives
self-acceptance = the ability to recognise your flaws without hating yourself
self-doubt = the feeling that you are not good enough or may fail
inferiority complex = a lasting belief that you are less valuable than others
midlife crisis = anxiety about identity and purpose in middle age
come out of your shell = to become less shy and more willing to talk to people
reinvent yourself = to change your image, habits or career in a significant way
personal growth = the process of improving your character, skills or self-knowledge
inner conflict = a struggle between two feelings, values or desires inside you
self-discipline = the ability to make yourself work or behave well without being forced
self-reliance = the ability to depend on your own efforts rather than on others
lack of confidence = not believing in your own abilities
impostor syndrome = the feeling that your success is undeserved and you will be found out
soul-searching = careful, honest thinking about your motives and values
sense of purpose = the feeling that your life has a meaningful direction
fulfil your potential = to achieve as much as you are capable of
live up to expectations = to be as good as people hoped or demanded
be true to yourself = to act according to your own values rather than other people's wishes
peer pressure = the influence of people your age to behave in a certain way
people-pleaser = someone who tries too hard to make others like them, often at a cost to themselves
comfort zone = a situation in which you feel safe and unchallenged
self-image = the idea you have of your own character and appearance
self-respect = pride in yourself that stops you accepting bad treatment
insecurity = a lack of confidence about yourself or your relationships
vulnerability = the state of being open to emotional hurt
self-pity = the habit of feeling sorry for yourself in an unhelpful way
bounce back = to recover quickly after a setback
integrity = the quality of being honest and sticking to your moral principles
prejudice = an unfair opinion formed without enough knowledge or experience
empathy = the ability to understand and share another person's feelings
stereotype = an oversimplified idea about a whole group of people
tolerance = willingness to accept behaviour and beliefs different from your own
bigotry = stubborn and unfair dislike of people who are different
unconscious bias = a hidden preference that affects judgement without you noticing
double standard = a rule applied more strictly to one group than to another
moral dilemma = a situation in which two ethical principles clash and both choices hurt someone
ethical dilemma = a difficult choice between two courses of action that both have moral costs
conscience = the inner sense of what is right and wrong
hypocrisy = claiming high moral standards while doing the opposite
altruism = unselfish concern for other people's welfare
civic duty = a responsibility you have as a member of society
human dignity = the idea that every person deserves respect simply for being human
stigmatise = to treat a person or group as shameful or unworthy
stand up for = to defend a person, idea or right, especially when it is unpopular
look down on = to think you are better than someone else
turn a blind eye = to ignore something wrong that you know is happening
take a stand = to state your position clearly and refuse to stay neutral
common ground = shared opinions or interests that make agreement possible
moral courage = the bravery to do what is right despite criticism or risk
compromise your principles = to act against your own moral beliefs for an advantage
hold a grudge = to keep feeling angry with someone for a long time after they hurt you
put yourself in someone else's shoes = to imagine how another person feels in their situation
personal values = the principles that guide your own choices and behaviour
conflicting loyalties = a situation in which two people or groups you care about want opposite things
bystander effect = the tendency not to help because you assume someone else will
social stigma = strong public disapproval attached to a person, condition or group
treat others with respect = to behave towards people in a way that recognises their worth
